study.notes: STUDY: STEP UP (NCT05646706), phase 3b randomised double blind placebo and active controlled trial at 95 sites in 11 countries of once weekly semaglutide 7.2 mg (dose_mg 7.2) vs semaglutide 2.4 mg vs placebo, 5:1:1, in adults with BMI 30 or more without diabetes, 72 weeks; 1407 randomised (1005, 201, 201), full analysis set, treatment policy estimand; Table 2 prints treatment comparisons for the 7.2 mg arm only (vs 2.4 mg and vs placebo), so the rows are semaglutide 7.2 mg vs placebo (route ci_95 for ETDs in native units, measure RR with log_RR_ci for the estimated treatment ratios to baseline of lipids, hsCRP and fasting insulin); the 2.4 mg vs placebo contrast is not printed and is not derived; supportive secondary endpoints (prespecified TRUE); pct_weight_change is the ETD vs placebo in percent weight change at week 72, minus 14.8 (95 percent CI minus 16.2 to minus 13.4; arms minus 18.7 vs minus 3.9); Table 1 baselines HbA1c 5.7 and 5.7 percent, eGFR 95.1 and 95.5 (geometric means), blood pressure and lipid baselines in the appendix; funded by Novo Nordisk (industry_funded TRUE); rob_overall low | BIBLIOGRAPHIC CORRECTION 2026-10-19: Identified 19 October from Europe PMC: Wharton S, Freitas P, Hjelmesaeth J, Kabisch M, et al, 'Once-weekly semaglutide 7.2 mg in adults with obesity (STEP UP)', Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2025. doi and pmid were NA and are supplied. NOTE for any later pass: a separate companion paper reports STEP UP T2D, doi 10.1016/s2213-8587(25)00225-6, pmid 40961953. This row is the obesity trial, population obesity and 72 weeks, not the T2D one, and the two must not be conflated.

json.design: STEP UP, phase 3b randomised double blind placebo and active controlled trial, semaglutide 7.2 mg vs 2.4 mg vs placebo 5:1:1, adults with obesity without diabetes, 1407 randomised, 72 weeks
json.reason: full text group (institutional route); nine inventory markers for semaglutide 7.2 mg vs placebo from Table 2 (ETDs with 95 percent CI and estimated treatment ratios to baseline with 95 percent CI); the 2.4 mg vs placebo contrast is not printed
other_markers: waist circumference, BMI, body weight in kg

rob.justification: double blind placebo controlled randomisation 5:1:1 (D1, D2 low); full analysis set with the treatment policy estimand (D3 low); laboratory outcomes (D4 low); registered trial with prespecified supportive secondary endpoints (D5 low)

doubts: only the 7.2 mg arm has printed contrasts vs placebo; the 2.4 mg arm is in the trial but not entered
ratios to baseline entered under measure RR by the existing convention; blood pressure, glucose, lipid and CRP baselines are in the appendix, not captured
